To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fatty acid transport in hepatocytes is stimulated by the proton gradient across the plasma membrane and is accelerated by an inwardly oriented H+ gradient.

1) fatty acid uptake in primary cultured rat liver cells follows an inwardly driven transmembrane proton concentration gradient; 2) the driving force for fatty acid uptake in hepatocytes is a proton gradient at the outer surface; 3) fatty acid uptake is stimulated by cellular acidosis, and 4) fatty acids further stimulate cellular recovery from acid loading.

the role of proton gradients on fatty acids uptake in primary cultured rat liver cells.
the effect of transmembrane pH on the uptake of fatty acids by hepatocytes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fatty acid uptake into hepatocytes follows an outwardly directed proton gradient and is accelerated by an inwardly driven proton gradient.
fatty acids are taken up in hepatocytes, at the very least, by a carrier mediated process, and that this carrier mediated process is influenced by transmembrane proton concentration gradients.
fatty acid uptake is stimulated by the transmembrane H+ gradient and by the presence of protons at both sides of the membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proton gradient is the driving force for fatty acid transport in the hepatocyte.

fatty acid uptake into hepatocytes is stimulated by intracellular alkalosis, which is caused by a paracellular acidosis, and by an acid load, which activates Na+/H+ exchange at the outer cell surface.
fatty acid uptake is increased by an outward proton gradient, which is created by cellular alkalinization, and is decreased by an inward proton gradient, which results from cellular acidification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fatty acids stimulate the activity of the Na+/H+-antiporter, and this effect is most pronounced during pHi recovery after an acid load.
the driving force for fatty acid influx in hepatocytes is an inwardly directed gradient for protons.
fatty acids stimulate Na(+)/H(+) antiporter activity, which is a mechanism that is well established in the regulation of cell pH homeostasis.
